question: Rabindranath Tagore started Santiniketan institute in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1901.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rabindranath Tagore founded his experimental school at Santiniketan (in Birbhum district, West Bengal) in 1901, beginning with only a handful of students in an open-air, nature-centred setting. (शांतिनिकेतन — 1901)

• The school was named Patha Bhavana and later grew into the university Visva-Bharati, which Tagore established in 1921; it became a Central University in 1951.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for Gitanjali, becoming the first non-European Nobel laureate in literature.

• He wrote India's national anthem "Jana Gana Mana" and Bangladesh's "Amar Sonar Bangla"; he renounced his knighthood after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919).

NOTE

• Santiniketan was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2023. Tagore's educational philosophy stressed learning in the open air, closeness to nature and the fusion of Indian and Western traditions.

question: Lomas Rishi cave is situated in which of the following Hills?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Barabar Hills.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Lomas Rishi cave is situated in the Barabar Hills of the Jehanabad district of Bihar, about 24 km north of Gaya. (लोमस ऋषि गुफा — बराबर पहाड़ियाँ, बिहार)

• The Barabar caves are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, dating to the Mauryan period (3rd century BCE).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Most of these caves were dedicated by Emperor Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha Maurya to the Ajivika sect.

• The Lomas Rishi cave is famous for its chaitya-arch doorway carved to imitate wooden construction, and for the mirror-like Mauryan polish on its interior walls.

NOTE

• The Barabar group (four caves) and the nearby Nagarjuni Hills (three caves) together represent the earliest phase of Indian rock-cut architecture, which later flowered at Ajanta, Ellora, Karle and Bhaja.

question: Archana wishes to contest for Lok Sabha elections in India. What is the maximum limit of constituencies that can she contest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Two.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Section 33(7) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, a candidate may contest an election from a maximum of two constituencies. (अधिकतम दो निर्वाचन क्षेत्र)

• If the candidate wins from both seats, Section 70 requires the person to resign one seat within 14 days, and a by-election is then held for the vacated seat.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Before the 1996 amendment, there was no such cap and a person could contest from any number of seats.

• Basic qualifications for the Lok Sabha (Article 84): the person must be a citizen of India, at least 25 years of age, and must fulfil other qualifications prescribed by Parliament.

NOTE

• The Election Commission of India (Article 324) conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President. It has recommended reducing the limit to a single constituency.

question: Nahid Siddiqui was awarded Milapfest's Lifetime Achievement Award in October 2017. She is recognized for which dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nahid Siddiqui is a celebrated exponent of the Kathak dance form. She received Milapfest's Lifetime Achievement Award in October 2017 for her contribution to Kathak. (कथक — नाहिद सिद्दीकी)

• Milapfest is a leading Indian arts development organisation based in the United Kingdom.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh); the name comes from "Katha" (story) and "Kathakar" (storyteller).

• Its main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh; it is marked by rapid chakkars (spins), intricate tatkar (footwork) and expressive abhinaya.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: What chemical element does "Mn" stand for in the science periodic table?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manganese.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The symbol "Mn" in the periodic table stands for Manganese, a hard, brittle, silvery-grey transition metal with atomic number 25. (मैंगनीज़ — Mn)

• Manganese is essential in steel-making (it removes oxygen and sulphur and adds hardness) and is used in dry cells and in the manufacture of ferro-manganese alloys.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The other options have different symbols: Magnesium = Mg (atomic number 12), Mendelevium = Md (101) and Molybdenum = Mo (42).

• India's chief manganese-producing states include Odisha, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra; the main ore is pyrolusite (MnO₂).

NOTE

• Frequently confused symbols in SSC: Na (Sodium), K (Potassium), Fe (Iron), Cu (Copper), Ag (Silver), Au (Gold), Sn (Tin), Pb (Lead), Sb (Antimony), W (Tungsten).

question: The moon moves around the earth in about ______ days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 27.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Moon completes one revolution around the Earth in about 27.3 days — this is called the sidereal month. (लगभग 27 दिन)

• The Moon also takes about 27.3 days to rotate once on its axis. Because its rotation and revolution periods are equal (synchronous rotation), we always see the same face of the Moon from the Earth.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The synodic month (new moon to new moon, i.e., the cycle of phases) is about 29.5 days, because the Earth also moves along its orbit in the meantime.

• The Moon is the Earth's only natural satellite; its light takes about 1.3 seconds to reach the Earth, and its average distance is about 3,84,400 km.

NOTE

• The Moon has no atmosphere and its gravity is about 1/6th of the Earth's. Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to soft-land near the lunar south pole (23 August 2023), now observed as National Space Day.

question: Which of the following articles of the Indian constitution provides for 'National commission for Scheduled Castes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 338.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 338 of the Constitution provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) — a constitutional body that investigates and monitors safeguards provided for the SCs. (अनुच्छेद 338 — राष्ट्रीय अनुसूचित जाति आयोग)

• The Commission consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three other members, appointed by the President.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 338A — National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (created by the 89th Amendment Act, 2003, which split the earlier joint commission).

• Article 338B — National Commission for Backward Classes (given constitutional status by the 102nd Amendment Act, 2018).

• Article 337 deals with special provision for educational grants for the Anglo-Indian community; Article 343 makes Hindi in Devanagari script the official language of the Union; Article 344 provides for the Official Language Commission.

NOTE

• Other constitutional bodies: UPSC (Art. 315), Election Commission (Art. 324), Finance Commission (Art. 280), CAG (Art. 148) and the Attorney General (Art. 76).

question: The historical Sher-Shah Suri Marg runs between _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi and Amritsar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The stretch of highway known today as Sher-Shah Suri Marg runs between Delhi and Amritsar — the north-western section of the historic Grand Trunk (GT) Road, formerly numbered NH-1. (शेरशाह सूरी मार्ग — दिल्ली से अमृतसर)

• It is named after Sher Shah Suri, the Sur ruler who rebuilt and extended this ancient highway in the 16th century.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The full Grand Trunk Road originally ran from Sonargaon (in present-day Bangladesh) through Delhi and Lahore up to Kabul (Afghanistan); Rudyard Kipling called it a "river of life" in Kim.

• Sher Shah planted shade trees, dug wells and built sarais (rest houses) along the road, and introduced the Rupiya (silver coin) and the Dak (postal) system.

NOTE

• Sher Shah Suri (1540–1545) defeated Humayun at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj/Bilgram (1540). His tomb is at Sasaram, Bihar. His revenue reforms later influenced Akbar's administration.

question: How many silver medals has won by India at Tokyo Olympics 2020 (played in 2021)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021), India won 2 silver medals, out of a total of 7 medals — its best-ever Olympic haul. (2 रजत पदक)

◦ Mirabai Chanu — silver in weightlifting (49 kg women's).

◦ Ravi Kumar Dahiya — silver in wrestling (57 kg freestyle).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India's full Tokyo tally: 1 gold (Neeraj Chopra, javelin throw — India's first-ever Olympic gold in athletics), 2 silver and 4 bronze.

• The bronze medals came from P. V. Sindhu (badminton), Lovlina Borgohain (boxing), Bajrang Punia (wrestling) and the men's hockey team, which won a medal after 41 years.

NOTE

• At the Paris Olympics 2024, India won 6 medals (1 silver, 5 bronze), with Neeraj Chopra taking silver in the javelin and Manu Bhaker winning two bronze medals in shooting.

question: Which famous female personality received the Padma Shri award for manipuri classical dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Elam Endira Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Elam Endira Devi, a distinguished exponent of the Manipuri classical dance form from Manipur, was honoured with the Padma Shri for her contribution to this art. (मणिपुरी नृत्य — एलम एंदिरा देवी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Manipuri is the classical dance of Manipur, based largely on the Raas Leela of Radha and Krishna; it is gentle and rounded in movement, with the female dancer wearing the distinctive stiff barrel-shaped skirt called the Kumil/Potloi.

• Its drum-based male dance is the vigorous Pung Cholom, and the martial-style dance is Thang-Ta.

NOTE

• The Padma awards — Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri — are announced on Republic Day and conferred by the President. The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award of India.

question: Which king was shown on his coins as a Veena player?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Samudragupta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gupta ruler Samudragupta (c. 335–380 CE) issued gold coins on which he is depicted playing the veena (lyre), showing his love of music and learning. (समुद्रगुप्त — वीणा वादक मुद्रा)

• Because of his extensive conquests, the historian V. A. Smith called him the "Napoleon of India".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• His achievements are recorded in the Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar Inscription), composed by his court poet Harisena in Sanskrit.

• Samudragupta's coin types include the Archer, Battle-axe, Ashvamedha, Tiger-slayer and Lyrist (Veena) types. He performed the Ashvamedha yajna.

• He was the son of Chandragupta I and the father of Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).

NOTE

• The Gupta period (c. 320–550 CE) is called the "Golden Age of India" for its achievements in art, literature (Kalidasa), mathematics (Aryabhata) and medicine, and for its purest gold coinage (dinaras).

question: Article 51A of the Indian constitution provides for ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fundamental Duties.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51A, in Part IV-A of the Constitution, lays down the Fundamental Duties of every citizen of India. (अनुच्छेद 51A — मूल कर्तव्य)

• They were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. Originally 10 in number, an 11th duty (providing education to children aged 6–14) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The idea of Fundamental Duties was borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by the courts, just like the Directive Principles.

• Examples: to abide by the Constitution, to cherish the ideals of the freedom struggle, to protect the sovereignty of India, to protect the environment and to develop the scientific temper.

NOTE

• Related parts: Part III (Articles 12–35) — Fundamental Rights; Part IV (Articles 36–51) — Directive Principles; Part IV-A (Article 51A) — Fundamental Duties; Part V — the Union (Executive, Parliament, Judiciary).

question: Which of the following profession is a type of seasonal unemployment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Farmer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Seasonal unemployment occurs when people are unable to find work during certain seasons of the year. Farmers and agricultural labourers are its classic example, because farm work is available mainly at the times of sowing and harvesting and is scarce in between. (मौसमी बेरोज़गारी — किसान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other occupations subject to seasonal unemployment include ice-factory workers, sugar-mill (khandsari) workers, tourist guides and construction labourers in the monsoon.

• Disguised unemployment is also common in Indian agriculture — more people work on a farm than are actually needed, so the marginal productivity of the extra workers is nearly zero.

NOTE

• Types of unemployment: Seasonal, Disguised, Structural, Cyclical, Frictional, Open, Educated and Technological. Government schemes such as MGNREGA (2005) guarantee 100 days of wage employment to rural households to reduce seasonal distress.

question: Limestone is a type of _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sedimentary rock.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Limestone is a sedimentary rock composed mainly of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃), formed from the accumulation and compaction of shells, corals and other marine remains on sea beds. (चूना पत्थर — अवसादी चट्टान)

• On metamorphism, limestone changes into marble.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sedimentary rocks are formed in layers (strata) by deposition and are the only rocks that contain fossils — examples: sandstone, shale, limestone, conglomerate.

• Igneous rocks form from the cooling of magma/lava (granite, basalt); metamorphic rocks form when existing rocks change under heat and pressure (marble, slate, gneiss, quartzite).

NOTE

• Uses of limestone: manufacture of cement, as a flux in blast furnaces for iron smelting, and in the making of lime. Karst topography, caves and stalactites are formed by the dissolution of limestone by rainwater.

question: Which country won the Women's Asia Cup 2022 of cricket?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India won the Women's Asia Cup 2022 (T20 format), held in Sylhet, Bangladesh, by defeating Sri Lanka by 8 wickets in the final on 15 October 2022. (महिला एशिया कप 2022 — भारत)

• It was India's 7th title in the Women's Asia Cup, and the team was led by Harmanpreet Kaur.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India has dominated the tournament, winning it in 2004, 2005, 2006, 2008, 2012, 2016 and 2022; Bangladesh won the 2018 edition.

• The Asia Cup is organised by the Asian Cricket Council (ACC), founded in 1983.

NOTE

• Indian women's cricket landmarks: runners-up at the 2017 ODI World Cup and the 2020 T20 World Cup; gold at the Asian Games 2023; and the launch of the Women's Premier League (WPL) in 2023.

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of "viviparous" animals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bird.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Viviparous animals are those that give birth to live young ones rather than laying eggs. Dogs, cats and cows are all viviparous mammals. (जरायुज जंतु)

• Birds are oviparous — they lay eggs, which develop and hatch outside the mother's body. Hence a bird is NOT viviparous.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Oviparous animals (egg-laying): birds, most reptiles, amphibians, fishes and insects.

• Ovoviviparous animals retain the eggs inside the body until they hatch — for example, some sharks and snakes.

• Exceptional mammals: the platypus and echidna (spiny anteater) are egg-laying mammals (monotremes).

NOTE

• In viviparous animals the embryo develops inside the mother and receives nourishment through the placenta; the chances of survival of the young are therefore much higher than in oviparous animals.

question: The transformation of the larva into an adult through drastic change is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is metamorphosis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Metamorphosis" is the biological process in which a larva changes into an adult through a series of drastic structural changes. (कायांतरण / रूपांतरण)

◦ Examples: tadpole → frog; caterpillar → pupa → butterfly; maggot → housefly.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Complete metamorphosis has four stages — egg, larva, pupa and adult (butterfly, housefly, mosquito, beetle).

• Incomplete metamorphosis has three stages — egg, nymph and adult (cockroach, grasshopper, dragonfly).

• In frogs, metamorphosis is controlled by the hormone thyroxine secreted by the thyroid gland; iodine deficiency stops the tadpole from becoming a frog.

NOTE

• Option 1 "budding" is a mode of asexual reproduction (in Hydra and yeast), in which a bud grows on the parent body and detaches to become a new individual.

question: The Ahom Kingdom in India was located in the ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmaputra valley.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ahom Kingdom was located in the Brahmaputra valley of present-day Assam. It was founded in 1228 CE by Sukapha, a Tai prince from Mong Mao (in present-day Myanmar/Yunnan). (अहोम साम्राज्य — ब्रह्मपुत्र घाटी, असम)

• The kingdom lasted for nearly 600 years, until it was annexed by the British after the Treaty of Yandabo (1826).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Ahoms famously defeated the Mughal army under Ram Singh I at the Battle of Saraighat (1671), in which the Ahom general Lachit Borphukan led a brilliant naval defence on the Brahmaputra.

• Sukapha's ascent is commemorated every year on 24 November as Asom Divas (Sukapha Divas); Lachit Divas is observed on 24 November as well in honour of the general's valour.

• The Ahom system of forced labour was called Paik, and their chronicles were called Buranjis.

NOTE

• The Ahom Moidams (burial mounds) of Charaideo, Assam, were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2024.

question: The Directive Principles of State Policy is included in which part of the Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part IV.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are contained in Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) of the Indian Constitution. (भाग IV — राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व)

• They were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland and are non-justiciable — i.e., they cannot be enforced in a court of law, but Article 37 declares them "fundamental in the governance of the country".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Part I (Articles 1–4) — the Union and its territory; Part II (Articles 5–11) — Citizenship; Part III (Articles 12–35) — Fundamental Rights.

• Important DPSPs: Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), Article 40 (organisation of village panchayats), Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code), Article 45 (early childhood care), Article 47 (prohibition of intoxicating drinks), Article 48A (protection of the environment) and Article 51 (promotion of international peace).

NOTE

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described the Directive Principles as a "novel feature" of the Constitution, and Granville Austin called the DPSPs and Fundamental Rights together the "conscience of the Constitution".

question: An annual allowance for wear and tear of a capital good is known as ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is depreciation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Depreciation" is the annual allowance made for the wear and tear, obsolescence and normal ageing of a capital good (such as machinery or a building). It is also called consumption of fixed capital. (मूल्यह्रास)

◦ Formula link: Net Investment = Gross Investment – Depreciation; NNP = GNP – Depreciation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "gross investment" is the total spending on new capital goods before deducting depreciation.

• Option 2 "devaluation" is a deliberate reduction in the external value of a country's currency by the government under a fixed exchange-rate system (India devalued the rupee in 1949, 1966 and 1991).

• Option 4 "disinvestment" is the sale of the government's equity stake in a public sector undertaking (handled by DIPAM).

NOTE

• Key national income identities: GDP (domestic output), GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad, NDP = GDP – depreciation, NNP at factor cost = National Income.

question: Indore gharana is one of the vocal gharanas of Indian classical music. It was founded by _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Amir Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indore gharana of Hindustani classical vocal music was founded by Ustad Amir Khan (1912–1974). (इंदौर घराना — उस्ताद अमीर खाँ)

• His style is famous for the vilambit (very slow) khayal, a meditative merukhand approach to note patterns, and clear sargam and taranas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ustad Amir Khan was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1971) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1967); he sang for films such as Baiju Bawra and Jhanak Jhanak Payal Baaje.

• Option 2 Doreswamy Iyengar was a veena maestro of Carnatic music; Option 3 Dr. L. Subramaniam is a celebrated violinist; Option 4 Ustad Bundu Khan was a sarangi player.

NOTE

• Major Hindustani vocal gharanas: Gwalior (the oldest), Agra, Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala, Rampur-Sahaswan, Bhendibazaar and Indore.

question: Guru Bipin Singh is associated with ________ dance form of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Bipin Singh (1918–2000) was the great guru of the Manipuri classical dance form, credited with systematising and popularising it — especially the solo form of Ras Leela — on the national stage. (मणिपुरी नृत्य — गुरु बिपिन सिंह)

• He trained the famous Jhaveri sisters (Nayana, Suverna, Ranjana and Darshana) and founded the Manipuri Nartanalaya.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Manipuri dance is devotional in character, centred on the Radha–Krishna Ras Leela, with soft, flowing, rounded movements and the accompanying drum dance Pung Cholom.

• Option 2 "Kalbelia" is a folk dance of the Kalbelia (snake-charmer) community of Rajasthan, inscribed in UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list (2010).

• Option 4 "Bachata" is a Latin American social dance from the Dominican Republic, not an Indian form.

NOTE

• Some noted dance gurus: Rukmini Devi Arundale (Bharatanatyam), Birju Maharaj (Kathak), Kelucharan Mohapatra (Odissi), Vempati Chinna Satyam (Kuchipudi) and Bipin Singh (Manipuri).

question: Diwali marks the day when lord Ram returned to Ayodhya after ______ years of exile after defeating king ravan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Diwali (Deepavali) commemorates the return of Lord Rama to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile (vanvas) and his victory over Ravana, the king of Lanka. The people of Ayodhya lit rows of earthen lamps (deepa + avali = a row of lamps) to welcome him. (14 वर्ष का वनवास)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Diwali falls on the Amavasya (new moon) of the Hindu month of Kartika, and the five-day festival includes Dhanteras, Naraka Chaturdashi, Lakshmi Puja, Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj.

• For Jains, Diwali marks the nirvana of Lord Mahavira (527 BCE); for Sikhs it is Bandi Chhor Divas, marking the release of Guru Hargobind from Gwalior fort.

NOTE

• The Ramayana was composed by Maharishi Valmiki; the Awadhi retelling Ramcharitmanas was written by Goswami Tulsidas. The Deepotsav of Ayodhya has repeatedly set Guinness World Records for the number of diyas lit.

question: As per the 2011 census of India, which Indian state has the lowest sex ratio?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, Haryana recorded the lowest sex ratio among the states — 879 females per 1,000 males. (हरियाणा — सबसे कम लिंगानुपात)

• The national sex ratio in 2011 was 943 females per 1,000 males.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kerala had the highest sex ratio among states (1,084), followed by Puducherry (1,037) among UTs; the lowest among all UTs was Daman and Diu (618).

• The child sex ratio (0–6 years) in 2011 was 919, the lowest since independence, with Haryana (834) again at the bottom.

NOTE

• The Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme was launched from Panipat, Haryana, on 22 January 2015 to address the declining child sex ratio. Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th since independence; its motto was "Our Census, Our Future".

question: Shiv Dayal Saheb, a banker from Agra, founded the Radha Soami Satsang in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1861.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shiv Dayal Saheb (Soamiji Maharaj), a banker of Agra, founded the Radha Soami Satsang in 1861. (राधा स्वामी सत्संग — 1861, आगरा)

• The movement teaches devotion to a living guru (Sant Satguru), the practice of Surat Shabd Yoga (union of the soul with the divine sound current), a vegetarian diet and abstention from intoxicants.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Radha Soami faith cuts across caste and creed and does not insist on external ritual; its main centres include Soami Bagh and Dayalbagh (Agra) and Beas (Punjab).

• It is counted among the 19th-century socio-religious reform movements of India, alongside the Brahmo Samaj (Raja Ram Mohan Roy, 1828), the Prarthana Samaj (1867), the Arya Samaj (Dayanand Saraswati, 1875) and the Ramakrishna Mission (Swami Vivekananda, 1897).

NOTE

• Other reform bodies often asked in SSC: the Theosophical Society (1875, Blavatsky and Olcott), the Aligarh Movement (Sir Syed Ahmad Khan), the Satyashodhak Samaj (Jyotiba Phule, 1873) and the Deoband Movement (1866).
